title: Oklahoma M3+ earthquakes of 2021-2026 are not a long aftershock tail: ETAS memory is not identifiable from the catalog and overpredicts 2021-2026 counts 4-5 times
abstract: Question: is the persistent 2021-2026 induced seismicity in Oklahoma a long aftershock (cascade) tail of the 2011-2016 sequence, or does it need a continuing external driver? Approach: we fit space-time ETAS models with a time-varying background (6-month bins or a 180-day time-smoothed kernel) to USGS ComCat M>=3 events (34.0-37.3 N, 99.6-95.9 W, 2010-2026; 3,119 events, 101 in 2021-2026). We tested identifiability with synthetic catalogs of known truth, made a predictive check with 200 simulated catalogs per fit, fit Omori-Utsu laws to the aftershock zones of the M>=4.8 mainshocks, and made forecasts from 2019 and 2021. Results: both fits are near-critical (branching ratio 1.55-1.99, p = 1.04-1.05) and assign 55-62% of the 2021-2026 events to descendants of pre-2017 events. But in synthetic catalogs with weak triggering (branching ratio 0.41) and a forcing on the same fault patches (0.5 km), the true share is 21-23% and the estimator returns 55-57%. Catalogs simulated from the fitted models give 411 (310-527) and 522 (382-691) events in 2021-2026 against 101 observed (0 of 200 simulations at or below). Omori tails of the Fairview, Pawnee, Cushing and 2014 Kansas mainshock zones explain about 22 of 378 M>=2.5 events (2-13% for p from 1.2 to free fits); the 2011 Prague zone had a new Mw 5.1 sequence in 2024. ETAS forecasts overpredicted 2019-2026 and 2021-2026 counts 5.2-10 times; exponential decay of recent counts was within a factor of 1.5. Conclusion: the residual seismicity occurs on the same faults but needs a decaying external driver, not cascade memory. Limitations: M>=3 only, 1-2 seeds per synthetic case, magnitude-type mix, 2-D kernels, one region, and a constructed forcing world.
